ITQAN:v3p266/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p266/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p266/r7.claim: The Qur'an favors the rarer of synonyms, such as ضيزى, الحطمة, سقر, لظى, and هاوية, often to preserve each surah's rhyme.
ITQAN:v3p266/r7.anchor: إيثار أغرب اللفظتين نحو ﴿ قسمة ضيزى ﴾ ولم يقل ( جائرة )

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r7.claim: The passage depicts cosmic upheaval and the collapse of social bonds; each person would offer even close family and tribe as ransom, while Hell burns and seizes those who evaded the call and hoarded wealth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p463/r7.anchor: The flames of Hell shall tear and burn his skin

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p268/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p268/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p268/r4.claim: Laza is either a name for Hell or for its second level; the transferred name means flame and is feminine, hence diptote.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p268/r4.anchor: لظى: اسم لجهنم، أو للدركة الثانية من دركاتها، وهو علم منقول من اللظى، وهو اللهب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p273/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p273/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p273/r11.claim: كلا rejects their wish to ransom themselves; in innaha, the pronoun is a matter-pronoun, and the grammatical analyses of laza and nizza'atan vary on the majority nominative reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p273/r11.anchor: كلا: ردع لودادتهم الافتداء وتنبيه على أنه لا ينفع.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r1.claim: He questions al-Zamakhshari's claim of an unspecified pronoun explained by its predicate, since a single word does not explain such a pronoun here.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p274/r1.anchor: ولا أدري ما هذا المضمر الذي ترجم عنه الخبر؟ وليس هذا من المواضع التي يفسر فيها المفرد الضمير

NAHHAS:v5p29/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p29/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p29/r13.claim: The pause after innahā laẓā is complete and good.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p148/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p148/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p148/r4.claim: Kalla decisively rebukes the criminal's wish: no ransom or imagined hope will ever produce escape.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366#3/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p366#3/r14.claim: كلا rejects the wish to ransom themselves; the verse then begins reporting about لظى, a layer of Hell, magnifying its horror.

ELMALILI:70:8-35/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:70:8-35/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:70:8-35/r6.claim: Lazā is a name for Hell, a blazing and engulfing fire.
ELMALILI:70:8-35/r6.anchor: alevli salgın ateş cehennemin bir ismi

FARRA:v3p183#2/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p183#2/r12.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p183#2/r12.claim: Laẓā is a proper name for Hell, which is why it is indeclinable.
FARRA:v3p183#2/r12.anchor: ولظى: اسم من أسماء جهنم فلذلك لم يجره.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r20.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r20.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r20.claim: Kallā rebukes the offender’s wish, warning that ransom will neither benefit nor rescue him from punishment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r20.anchor: { كلا } رد للمجرم عن الودادة ، وتنبيه على أنه لا ينفعه الافتداء ولا ينجيه من العذاب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r21.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r21.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r21.claim: The pronoun in innahā refers to the Fire although it has not been named, since punishment implies it; alternatively it is an indefinite pronoun explained by its predicate or a pronoun of the matter.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r21.anchor: والضمير للنار ، ولم يجر لها ذكر ؛ لأن ذكر العذاب دل عليها . ويجوز أن يكون ضميرا مبهما ترجم عنه الخبر ، أو ضمير القصة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r22.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r22.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r22.claim: Lazā is either the Fire’s proper name, transferred from laẓā meaning flame, or simply means flame.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p612/r22.anchor: { لظى } علم للنار ، منقول من اللظى : بمعنى اللهب . ويجوز أن يراد اللهب

RAZI-FULL:v30p112#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p112#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p112#3/r1.claim: Kallā rebukes the sinner’s wish to ransom his children and declares that ransom cannot help or save him from punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v30p112#3/r1.anchor: كلا } ردع للمجرم عن كونه بحيث يود الافتداء ببنيه ، وعلى أنه لا ينفعه ذلك الافتداء

RAZI-FULL:v30p112#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p112#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p112#3/r2.claim: One view takes the pronoun as referring to the Fire, understood from the prior mention of punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v30p112#3/r2.anchor: أن هذا الضمير للنار ، ولم يجر لها ذكر إلا أن ذكر العذاب دل عليها

RAZI-FULL:v30p112#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p112#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p112#3/r3.claim: Alternatively, it is the pronoun of the story; laẓā is a name of the Fire.
RAZI-FULL:v30p112#3/r3.anchor: يجوز أن يكون ضمير القصة ، ولظى من أسماء النار

RAZI-FULL:v30p112#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p112#3/r4.speaker: الليث
RAZI-FULL:v30p112#3/r4.claim: Al-Layth glosses laẓā as a clear flame and gives the verb forms laẓat, talaẓẓā, and talaẓẓat.

RAZI-FULL:v30p112#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p112#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p112#3/r5.claim: Laẓā is a proper name for the Fire, derived from flame; as a definite proper noun it is diptote and therefore has no tanwīn.
RAZI-FULL:v30p112#3/r5.anchor: ولظى علم للنار منقول من اللظى ، وهو معرفة لا ينصرف ، فلذلك لم ينون

STUDYQURAN:70:15/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:15/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:70:15/r1.claim: “Nay” denies the possibility of ransom mentioned in the preceding verses.
STUDYQURAN:70:15/r1.anchor: Nay denies the possibility of ransom mentioned in the previous verses

STUDYQURAN:70:15/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:15/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:70:15/r2.claim: Alternatively, the opening may be translated “Truly it is a churning fire.”
STUDYQURAN:70:15/r2.anchor: Alternately, the verse could be translated, “Truly it is a churning fire” (Q)

STUDYQURAN:70:15/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:70:15/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:70:15/r3.claim: Laẓā is a name for Hell because its flames churn.
STUDYQURAN:70:15/r3.anchor: Churning fire translates laẓā, which is considered one of the names of Hell

TABATABAI:70:11-18/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r15.claim: Kallā rebukes the hope of escape by ransom. The pronoun refers to Hell or the Fire, called Laẓā because it blazes; it burns and tears away extremities and pursues criminals, so no ransom diverts it.
TABATABAI:70:11-18/r15.anchor: كلا للردع، وضمير { إنها } لجهنم أو للنار وسميت لظى لكونها تتلظى وتشتعل

BURSEVI:v10p122/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p122/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p122/r8.claim: كلا rebukes the wish and declares rescue impossible: the criminal's darkened condition through sin has earned punishment.
BURSEVI:v10p122/r8.anchor: ردع للمجرم عن الودادة وتصريح بامتناع إنجاء الافتداء أي لا يكون كما يتمنى

BURSEVI:v10p122/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p122/r9.speaker: القرطبي
BURSEVI:v10p122/r9.claim: Al-Qurtubi allows كلا to mean either rebuke or indeed; on the latter reading, ينجيه closes the preceding sentence and كلا starts the next.
BURSEVI:v10p122/r9.anchor: وعن القرطبي أن كلا يكون بمعنى الردع وبمعنى حقا وكلا الوجهين جائز

BURSEVI:v10p122/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p122/r10.speaker: المحققون
BURSEVI:v10p122/r10.claim: The authorities and the Sajawandi stopping mark favor the rebuke reading, placing an unrestricted pause at كلا.
BURSEVI:v10p122/r10.anchor: والمحققون على الأول ومن ذلك وضع السجاوندي علامة الوقف المطلق على كلا

BURSEVI:v10p122/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p122/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p122/r11.claim: The pronoun refers to Hell, indicated by the preceding mention of punishment.
BURSEVI:v10p122/r11.anchor: أي النار المدلول عليها بذكر العذاب والمراد جهنم

BURSEVI:v10p122/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p122/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p122/r12.claim: Laza is a name for the Fire or its second level, derived from a pure, smokeless flame; alternatively it means such a flame directly and denotes extreme burning.
BURSEVI:v10p122/r12.anchor: وهو علم للنار وللدرك الثاني منها منقول من اللظى بمعنى الهب الخالص

TABRISI:70:15-16/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:70:15-16/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:70:15-16/r10.claim: Laẓā is a name for Hell, derived from blazing.
TABRISI:70:15-16/r10.anchor: لظى اسم من أسماء جهنم مأخوذة من التوقد

TABRISI:70:15-16/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:70:15-16/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:70:15-16/r13.claim: Al-mawaddah can mean either wishing for something or loving it.
TABRISI:70:15-16/r13.anchor: اللغة: المودة مشتركة بين التمني وبين المحبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r11.claim: Laẓā is a proper feminine name of Hell, definite and indeclinable, so it receives no tanwīn.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r11.anchor: ولظى من أسماء النار نعوذ بالله منها، وهي معرفة لا تنصرف؛ فلذلك لا تنون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r12.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r12.claim: Al-Layth defines laẓā as a pure flame.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r13.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r13.claim: The source gives the verbal forms laẓiyat al-nāru talazzā laẓan and talaẓẓat talaẓẓiyan.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r14.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p216/r14.claim: The word also occurs in the phrase “a fire that blazes.”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r5.claim: Verses 15–16 warn of hell's severe punishment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:70:8/r5.anchor: 15 ve 16. âyetler cehennemin şiddetli azabını hatırlatmakta

BURHAN:v1p75/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p75/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p75/r6.claim: The sequence ending with “it calls whoever turned away and turned back” is another example of these fawāṣil.
BURHAN:v1p75/r6.anchor: كلا إنها لظى نزاعة للشوى تدعو من أدبر وتولى وجمع فأوعى

ITQAN:v3p98/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p98/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p98/r1.claim: In this metaphor class one side is literal and the other figurative: fire's 'calling' is figurative, and Hell as the mother of sinners is a refuge and return like a human mother sheltering her child.

AKHFASH:v2p549/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p549/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p549/r2.claim: Alternatively, laẓā may be nominative as the predicate of inna, with an-nazzāʿa nominative as a new subject.
AKHFASH:v2p549/r2.anchor: وان شئت جعلت {لظى} رفعا على خبر {إن} ورفعت "النزاعة" على الابتداء

MAJAZ:v2p269/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p269/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p269/r4.claim: For humans, shawāt are the hands, feet, and head; al-Aʿshā’s word shawātahu is corrected by Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ to sarātahu.
MAJAZ:v2p269/r4.anchor: واحدتها شواة وهى اليدان والرجلان والرأس من الآدميين

MAJAZ:v2p269/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p269/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p269/r5.claim: He reports hearing a man in Medina say iqshaʿarrat shawātī, my limbs bristled, as evidence for the human use of shawā.
MAJAZ:v2p269/r5.anchor: وسمعت رجلا من أهل المدينة يقول اقشعرت شواتى

MAJAZ:v2p269/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p269/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p269/r6.claim: For a horse, shawā means its legs, as in ʿablu al-shawā; it is not used for the head, since horses are praised for slender cheeks and a refined face.
MAJAZ:v2p269/r6.anchor: ولا يكون هذا للرأس لأنهم وصفوا الخيل بأسالة الخدين وعتق الوجه ورقته

SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r11.claim: كلا is a rebuke and deterrent against imagining ransom will work.
SAMIN-DURR:70:13-14/r11.anchor: و " كلا " ردع وزجر عن اعتقاد ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:70:15/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:15/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:70:15/r1.claim: The pronoun in إنها may refer implicitly to the Fire, inferred from عذاب; it may instead be a story pronoun or an indefinite pronoun explained by what follows.
SAMIN-DURR:70:15/r1.anchor: في الضمير ثلاثة أوجه، أحدها: أنه ضمير النار، وإن لم يجر لها ذكر لدلالة لفظ " عذاب " عليها

SAMIN-DURR:70:15/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:15/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:70:15/r2.claim: If the pronoun means the Fire, لظى may be its predicate, with نزاعة as a second predicate or predicate of omitted هي; alternatively لظى is apposition and نزاعة the predicate of إن.

SAMIN-DURR:70:15/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:15/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:70:15/r3.claim: If the pronoun is a story or indefinite pronoun, لظى نزاعة is a subject-predicate clause serving as إن's predicate and explaining it.
SAMIN-DURR:70:15/r3.anchor: وعلى الثاني يكون " لظى نزاعة " جملة من مبتدأ وخبر، في محل الرفع خبرا ل " إن "

SAMIN-DURR:70:15/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:15/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:70:15/r5.claim: The commentator challenges al-Zamakhsharī's indefinite-pronoun analysis; the author replies that one word must explain it, either لظى or نزاعة.
SAMIN-DURR:70:15/r5.anchor: قال الشيخ بعد حكايته الثالث عن الزمخشري: " ولا أدري ما هذا المضمر الذي ترجم عنه الخبر؟

SAMIN-DURR:70:15/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:15/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:70:15/r6.claim: An indefinite pronoun cannot be explained by the whole clause لظى نزاعة, since that collapses this analysis into the story-pronoun view; only a pronoun of شأن or قصة is explained by a clause.
SAMIN-DURR:70:15/r6.anchor: لئلا يتحد القولان، أعني هذا القول وقول إنها ضمير القصة، ولم يعهد ضمير مفسر بجملة

SAMIN-DURR:70:15#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:70:15#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:70:15#2/r7.claim: لظى originally means flame and became a name for Hell, which is why it is diptote.
SAMIN-DURR:70:15#2/r7.anchor: واللظى في الأصل: اللهب. ونقل علما لجهنم، ولذلك منع من الصرف

ZAJJAJ:v5p220#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p220#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p220#2/r2.claim: Kallā is a rebuke and an alert, meaning that none of these people will return, so take heed.
ZAJJAJ:v5p220#2/r2.anchor: (كلا) ردع وتنبيه، أي لا يرجع أحد من هؤلاء فاعتبروا

ZAJJAJ:v5p220#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p220#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p220#2/r3.claim: The passage names the Fire as laẓā.

ASAD-NOTES:70:15/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:70:15/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:70:15/r1.claim: The punishment awaiting the sinner is a raging flame.
ASAD-NOTES:70:15/r1.anchor: Verily, all [that awaits him] is a raging flame

ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#4/r1.claim: Kallā rebukes the criminal for his wish and states that escape is impossible.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#4/r1.anchor: ردع للمجرم عن الودادة وتصريح بامتناع الإنجاء

ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#4/r2.claim: The pronoun in innahā refers to the fire implied by the mention of punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#4/r2.anchor: ﴿ إنها ﴾ للنار المدلول عليها بذكر العذاب

ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#4/r3.claim: Laẓā is the predicate of inna and a proper name for Hell or its second level, derived from “flame”; it is diptote as a feminine proper name.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#4/r3.anchor: ﴿ لظى ﴾ خبر أن وهي علم لجهنم أو للدركة الثانية من دركاتها منقول من اللظى بمعنى اللهب الخالص ومنع الصرف للعلمية والتأنيث

ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#4/r4.claim: Alternatively, laẓā means flame by hyperbole, as though the whole fire were pure flame.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#4/r4.anchor: وجوز أن يراد اللهب على المبالغة كان كلها لهب خالص

ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#4/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#4/r5.claim: The missing tanwīn may reflect treating connected speech like a pause, or treating the word as a generic proper name shifted from a form with al-, like saḥar for a particular dawn.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p60#4/r5.anchor: وحذف التنوين إما لإجراء الوصل مجرى الوقف أو لأنه علم جنس معدول عما فيه اللام كسحر إذا أردت سحرا بعينه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r15.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r15.claim: Nothing can save him from God's punishment; Baghawi then begins a new statement identifying laẓā as Hell.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r15.anchor: {كلا} لا ينجيه من عذاب الله شيء ثم ابتدأ فقال: {إنها لظى}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r16.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r16.claim: Laẓā is one of the names of Hell.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r16.anchor: {إنها لظى} وهي اسم من أسماء جهنم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r17.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r17.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r17.claim: Another view makes Laẓā the second level of Hell, named for its blazing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p222/r17.anchor: وقيل: هي الدركة الثانية سميت بذلك لأنها تتلظى أي: تتلهب.

BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r5.claim: The rebuke dissuades the criminal from wishing for ransom and declares that ransom will not save him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r5.anchor: ردع للمجرم عن الودادة ودلالة على أن الافتداء لا ينجيه

BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r6.claim: The pronoun refers to the Fire, or is an indefinite pronoun explained by laẓā; alternatively it refers to the affair, with laẓā as subject.
BAYDAWI-FULL:70:13-17/r6.anchor: الضمير للنار أو مبهم يفسره { لظى } وهو خبر أو بدل أو للقصة و { لظى } مبتدأ

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاعبداللهمنطلقحدثنابذل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاعبداللهمنطلقحدثنابذل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاعبداللهمنطلقحدثنابذل.claim: Sībawayh cites Q 70:15–16, ‘it is a blazing fire, seizing the scalp,’ as a Quranic example in the discussion of raised predicates.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاعبداللهمنطلقحدثنابذل.anchor: وقال الله عز وجل @QB@ كلا إنها لظى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r7.claim: Kalla rejects the criminal’s imagined ransom, whether an unspoken wish known to God or a voiced hope; the estimate is: no ransom and no rescue.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r7.anchor: يقال له كلا ، أي لا افتداء ولا إنجاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r8.claim: “It is a blaze” begins an explanatory resumption prompted by kalla’s rejection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r8.anchor: استئناف بياني ناشىء عما أفاده حرف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r9.claim: The feminine pronoun refers to the sight of Hell that the criminal sees before him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r9.anchor: عائد إلى ما يشاهده المجرم قبالته من مرأى جهنم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r10.claim: The pronoun is feminine because laẓā has feminine alif; the following descriptions predicate further qualities of it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r10.anchor: مقترنا بألف التأنيث أنث الضمير باعتبار تأنيث الخبر واتبع اسمها بأوصاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p162/r11.claim: The description implies that the blaze is prepared for the criminal: it burns him and strips away his scalp.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#6/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#6/r1.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#6/r1.claim: Lazā is one of Hell's names and therefore takes no tanwīn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#6/r1.anchor: قال الفراء هو اسم من أسماء جهنم فلذلك لم يجر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#6/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#6/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#6/r2.claim: Others gloss it as a pure flame; Ibn al-Anbārī says it is named for its intense burning.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#6/r2.anchor: وقال غيره معناها في اللغة اللهب الخالص وقال ابن الانباري سميت لظى لشدة توقدها وتلهبها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#6/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#6/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#6/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī cites talaẓẓā for blazing and burning, illustrated by a verse describing an unrelenting Fire.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p361#6/r3.anchor: يقال هو يتلظى أي يتلهب ويتوقد وكذلك النار تتلظى يراد بها هذا المعنى وأنشدوا جحيما تلظى لا تفتر ساعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225/r5.claim: Lazā describes Hell and its intense heat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p225/r5.anchor: وقوله: {إنها لظى} يصف النار وشدة حرها

JISHUMI:v10p7077/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7077/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7077/r14.claim: Laẓā is a name of Hell derived from blazing, as in the fire that blazes intensely.
JISHUMI:v10p7077/r14.anchor: ولظى: اسم من أسماء جهنم مأخوذ من التوقد، ومنه: (فأنذرتكم نارا تلظى).

JISHUMI:v10p7078/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r1.claim: Kallā may derive from kadhā lā, reduced and doubled for emphasis, or mean “indeed.”
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r1.anchor: و (كلا): قيل: أصله: كذا لا، فخففوه وشددوه للمبالغة، فصار (كلا)، وقيل: معناه: حقا.

JISHUMI:v10p7078/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r3.claim: Laẓā is inna’s predicate and nazzāʿa a second predicate; alternatively the pronoun is support and laẓā the subject.
JISHUMI:v10p7078/r3.anchor: لظى موضعها رفع، لأنها خبر (إن)، ونزاعة خبر آخر، ويجوز أن تكون الهاء في إنها عماد،

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r17.claim: Lazā may be one of Hell's names, because it blazes with intense heat.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r17.anchor: أحدهما : أنها اسم من أسماء جهنم , سميت بذلك لأنها التي تتلظى , وهو اشتداد حرها .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r18.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r18.claim: Al-Dahhak says Lazā is the eighth level of Hell.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p91/r18.anchor: الثاني : أنه اسم الدرك الثامن في جهنم , قاله الضحاك .

MUQATIL:70:8-18/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:70:8-18/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:70:8-18/r10.claim: No ransom saves him; the blazing Fire stretches out and has power over them.
MUQATIL:70:8-18/r10.anchor: يقول الله تعالى: { كلا } لا ينجيه ذلك لو افتدى بهذا كله، ثم استأنف فقال: { إنها لظى } [آية: 15] يعني بلظى استطالتها وقدرتها عليهم يعني النار

NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#6/r1.claim: “كلا” rebukes the criminal's wish to ransom himself and warns that ransom cannot benefit him or save him from punishment.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#6/r1.anchor: ردع للمجرم عن الودادة وتنبيه على أنه لا ينفعه الافتداء ولا ينجيه من العذاب

NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#6/r2.claim: The pronoun may refer to the Fire indicated by “العذاب,” to the people as explained by its predicate, or be an implicit pronoun of the matter.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#6/r2.anchor: إنا النار ودل ذكر العذاب عليها أو هو ضمير منهم ترجم عنه الخبر أو ضمير القصة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#6/r3.claim: “لظى” is the proper name of the Fire.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p279#6/r3.anchor: أو ضمير القصة ﴿ لظى ﴾ علم النار

QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r1.claim: Kalla can mean indeed, completing the preceding sentence at ينجيه, or no, completing the sentence there to deny that ransom can save him.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r1.anchor: وهي هنا تحتمل الأمرين فإذا كانت بمعنى حقا كان تمام الكلام «ينجيه». وإذا كانت بمعنى لا

QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r2.claim: Laza is Hell, whose flames blaze; the wording is linked to the fire that blazes in 92:14.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r2.anchor: أي هي جهنم أي تتلظى نيرانها

QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r3.claim: The word is derived from talazzī: iltizāʾ is a fire's ignition, and talazzī is its blazing.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r3.anchor: واشتقاق لظي من التلظي. والتظاء النار التهابها، وتلظيها تلهبها.

QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r4.claim: Another etymology derives the name from an original laẓẓ, denoting the duration of its punishment, with one emphatic consonant changed to a long alif.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r4.anchor: وقيل: كان أصلها «لظظ» أي مادامت لدوام عذابها فقلبت إحدى الظائين ألفا فبقيت لظى.

QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r5.claim: Another view identifies Laza as the second level among the levels of Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r5.anchor: وقيل: هي الدركة الثانية من طبقات جهنم.

QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r6.claim: Laza is a definite feminine proper name and therefore does not decline.
QURTUBI-FULL:70:15-16/r6.anchor: وهي اسم مؤنث معرفة فلا ينصرف.
